questions.question: In which of the following provinces did NOT have the 'Zabt' system during Akbar's time due to difficulties in land inspection?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengal and Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Zabt system** was a land revenue system introduced during the reign of **Akbar** under the supervision of his finance minister **Raja Todar Mal**.
 
• The system involved the measurement of agricultural land and fixing the revenue based on the average produce and prices over the past 10 years.
 
• While the **Zabt system** was widely implemented in most provinces of the Mughal Empire, it could not be applied effectively in **Bengal and Gujarat** due to the following challenges:
 
 
• **Bengal**: The region had a complex riverine landscape, with frequent floods and shifting river courses making land measurement extremely difficult.
 
• **Gujarat**: The region had diverse agricultural practices and terrains, which posed challenges to the uniform application of the Zabt system.
 
 
 
• Instead of Zabt, other systems like **Kankut** or **Nasaq** were used in these areas to estimate land revenue.
 
• This highlights the adaptability of the Mughal administration in modifying their policies based on regional conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zabt System:**

 
 
• This system was a crucial part of Akbar's revenue reforms and was based on the principles of standardizing land revenue collection.
 
• The system required accurate land measurement, categorization of land based on fertility, and fixation of revenue rates based on average produce and prices.
 
• It aimed at maximizing revenue collection while ensuring fairness and reducing the burden on peasants.
 
• The assessment was conducted in a scientific manner, with records maintained for future references.
 
 
 
• **Kankut System:**
 
 
• The **Kankut** system was another land revenue assessment method used in regions where accurate land measurement was not feasible.
 
• Under this system, the estimation of revenue was done based on the **inspection of standing crops** or mutual agreements between farmers and revenue officers.
 
• It was less precise than Zabt but provided a flexible alternative in challenging terrains.
 
 
 
• **Nasaq System:**
 
 
• **Nasaq** was another revenue collection method employed in areas with irregular agricultural activities.
 
• Revenue was determined based on past practices or mutual agreements rather than strict measurement or assessments.
 
• This system was often used in **Bengal and Gujarat**, where local conditions demanded flexibility.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Bengal and Gujarat:**
 
 
• **Bengal**: Frequent flooding, alluvial soil changes, and the deltaic region's dynamic geography made it difficult to implement Zabt.
 
• **Gujarat**: The diversity in agricultural practices, including cash crops like cotton, and the arid regions posed challenges to standardized revenue assessment.
 
• Both regions required alternative methods to ensure effective revenue collection and avoid overburdening the population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Raja Todar Mal's Reforms:**

 
 
• As Akbar's finance minister, **Raja Todar Mal** introduced several revenue reforms to streamline the administration.
 
• He emphasized accurate land measurement, categorized land based on fertility, and standardized revenue rates.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations:**
 
 
• The Mughal administration showed remarkable adaptability in modifying revenue systems to suit regional conditions.
 
• This flexibility helped maintain stability and ensured efficient revenue collection across the empire.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The Zabt system and other revenue reforms laid the foundation for subsequent revenue systems during British rule in India.
 
• It demonstrated the importance of scientific and fair revenue practices in maintaining administrative efficiency and peasant welfare.

questions.question: Seventh Schedule of the Indian constitution deals with the ____________.

options.text: Power, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats
Power, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union, State and Concurrent Lists**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** contains three lists: the **Union List**, the **State List**, and the **Concurrent List**, which delineate the division of powers between the Union and State governments.
 
• The **Union List** includes subjects of national importance such as defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, banking, and communications. Only the **Parliament** has the exclusive power to legislate on these matters.
 
• The **State List** comprises subjects of local or state importance such as police, public health, agriculture, and irrigation. Only the **State Legislature** can make laws on these topics.
 
• The **Concurrent List** includes subjects of mutual interest to both the Union and States, such as education, forests, trade unions, and marriage. Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate on these matters. However, in case of a conflict, the law made by the Parliament prevails.
 
• The division of powers under the Seventh Schedule ensures the federal structure of India, where both the Union and State governments operate within their defined jurisdictions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union List:**

 
 
• It contains **100 subjects** (originally 97), including areas of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• Only the **Parliament** is empowered to make laws on these subjects.
 
• Examples: **Currency, Citizenship, and International Trade.**
 
 
 
• **State List:**
 
 
• It contains **61 subjects** (originally 66), including areas of state and local importance like police, public health, and agriculture.
 
• The **State Legislature** has exclusive powers to legislate on these subjects.
 
• Examples: **Law and Order, Fisheries, and Markets.**
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• It contains **52 subjects** (originally 47), which are of joint interest to both the Union and States.
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws, the **Union law prevails**.
 
• Examples: **Education, Marriage, and Bankruptcy.**
 
 
 
• **Residue Powers:**
 
 
• Any subject not mentioned in the three lists falls under **residuary powers**, which are vested in the **Union Government**.
 
• Examples: **Cyber Laws, Space Research, and Internet-based issues.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amendments:**

 
 
• The subjects in the lists can be amended by the **Parliament** under **Article 368**.
 
• For example, the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 transferred **Education** from the State List to the Concurrent List.
 
 
 
• **Federal Structure:**
 
 
• The Seventh Schedule is a cornerstone of India's **quasi-federal structure**, ensuring a balance between centralization and decentralization.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• Any legislation passed by the Union or State that violates the distribution of powers can be challenged in the **Supreme Court** or **High Courts**.

questions.question: Which of the following amendment act of the Indian constitution replaced the term "internal disturbance" with "armed rebellion" in the context of a national emergency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44th Amendment Act, 1978**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **44th Amendment Act, 1978** replaced the term **"internal disturbance"** with **"armed rebellion"** in Article 352 of the Constitution of India.
 
• This amendment was introduced to restrict the scope of declaring a **national emergency**, ensuring it could not be misused for political purposes.
 
• The term **"internal disturbance"** was considered vague and susceptible to misuse, whereas **"armed rebellion"** is more specific and denotes severe internal conflict involving armed forces.
 
• The change was part of the reforms aimed at safeguarding democratic principles after the misuse of emergency powers during the **1975-77 Emergency** declared under the leadership of then Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• The 44th Amendment Act also introduced other provisions to make it harder to impose a national emergency, such as requiring the written recommendation of the Cabinet before the President could proclaim an emergency.

questions.question: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations was established in which of the following places?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangkok**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)** was established on **8 August 1967** in **Bangkok, Thailand**, through the signing of the **Bangkok Declaration** (also known as the ASEAN Declaration).
 
• The founding members of ASEAN include **Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore,** and **Thailand**, who signed the Bangkok Declaration to promote economic cooperation, cultural exchange, and regional stability.
 
• The **Bangkok Declaration** emphasized the principles of equality, partnership, and mutual respect among the member nations, forming the foundation for ASEAN’s objectives.
 
• The main goals of ASEAN are to accelerate **economic growth**, promote **social progress**, and ensure **regional peace and stability**.
 
• The ASEAN Secretariat, which facilitates the coordination of activities and implementation of decisions, is located in **Jakarta, Indonesia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Bangkok Declaration:**

 
 
• The Bangkok Declaration is the founding document of ASEAN, signed on **8 August 1967**.
 
• It laid the foundation for cooperation in various fields such as **economic development, social progress, cultural exchange, and regional stability**.
 
• It emphasized the importance of **non-interference** in the internal affairs of member states and the promotion of **peaceful dispute resolution**.
 
 
 
• **ASEAN Member States:**
 
 
• Initially, ASEAN had **5 founding members**: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.
 
• Over time, additional countries joined ASEAN, including **Brunei (1984), Vietnam (1995), Laos and Myanmar (1997), and Cambodia (1999)**, bringing the total membership to **10**.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of ASEAN:**
 
 
• To accelerate **economic growth, social progress, and cultural development** in the region.
 
• To promote **regional peace and stability** through respect for justice and the rule of law.
 
• To foster collaboration in various sectors such as **trade, agriculture, industry, transportation, and education**.
 
 
 
• **ASEAN Charter:**
 
 
• The **ASEAN Charter** was signed in **2007** and came into effect in **2008**.
 
• It provides a legal framework and institutional structure for ASEAN, making it a rules-based organization.
 
• It established key bodies such as the **ASEAN Summit** and the **ASEAN Coordinating Council**.
 
 
 
• **Important Summits:**
 
 
• The **ASEAN Summit** is held **annually** and involves the leaders of member states discussing regional issues and cooperation.
 
• Key agreements such as the establishment of the **ASEAN Economic Community (AEC)** have been signed during these summits.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Bangkok:**

 
 
• Bangkok, the capital city of **Thailand**, holds historical importance as the birthplace of ASEAN.
 
• The signing of the **Bangkok Declaration** in this city laid the foundation for regional cooperation in Southeast Asia.
 
 
 
• **ASEAN Economic Community (AEC):**
 
 
• The AEC was established in **2015** to create a single market and production base among ASEAN countries.
 
• It aims to promote the free flow of goods, services, investment, skilled labor, and capital.
 
 
 
• **ASEAN’s Global Influence:**
 
 
• ASEAN has established partnerships with major global powers such as the **United States, China, Japan, India,** and the **European Union**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in regional forums like the **East Asia Summit** and **ASEAN Regional Forum**.

questions.question: In January 2025, who has been appointed as the CEO of the Delhi Waqf Board?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Azimul Haque**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Azimul Haque** has been appointed as the **CEO of the Delhi Waqf Board** in **January 2025**. This appointment is significant as the Delhi Waqf Board plays a crucial role in managing waqf properties and ensuring their proper utilization.
 
• The **Delhi Waqf Board** is a statutory body established under the **Waqf Act, 1995**, which governs waqf properties and related matters in India.
 
• **Azimul Haque** is known for his extensive administrative experience and in-depth understanding of waqf properties, making him an ideal choice for this role.
 
• The CEO of the Waqf Board is responsible for overseeing the management, preservation, and development of waqf properties and ensuring their compliance with legal and administrative frameworks.
 
• This appointment aligns with the government's commitment to strengthening the functioning of statutory bodies like the Waqf Board and ensuring transparency and accountability in their operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Delhi Waqf Board:**

 
 
• The Delhi Waqf Board is responsible for managing waqf properties in the region, which include mosques, graveyards, dargahs, and other charitable institutions.
 
• It ensures that waqf properties are used for purposes aligned with Islamic principles, such as education, welfare, and religious activities.
 
• The Board also takes steps to prevent encroachments and misuse of waqf properties and ensures their proper maintenance and revenue generation.
 
 
 
• **Waqf Act, 1995:**
 
 
• The Waqf Act, 1995, is a central legislation enacted to provide for the administration and supervision of waqf properties in India.
 
• The Act defines waqf as a permanent dedication of movable or immovable property by a Muslim for religious, pious, or charitable purposes.
 
• It establishes Waqf Boards at the state level to manage and regulate waqf properties in their respective jurisdictions.
 
 
 
• **Role of the CEO:**
 
 
• The CEO of the Waqf Board is a key administrative position responsible for implementing policies, managing staff, and ensuring the proper functioning of the Board.
 
• The CEO also liaises with government agencies, legal authorities, and other stakeholders to address issues related to waqf properties.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Waqf Management:**
 
 
• Encroachments on waqf properties and illegal occupation are major challenges faced by Waqf Boards across India.
 
• Limited financial resources and lack of skilled personnel often hinder the effective management and development of waqf properties.
 
• Efforts are being made to digitize records and introduce modern management practices to address these challenges.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Encroachment Issues:** Waqf Boards in India have been facing challenges due to widespread encroachments on waqf properties. Ensuring proper legal action and recovery of these properties is a major priority for the Board.
 
• **Digitization:** The Government of India has initiated efforts to digitize waqf records under the **Waqf Management System of India (WAMSI)** to improve transparency and accountability.
 
• **Role of Central Waqf Council:** The Central Waqf Council provides guidance and oversight to state Waqf Boards and also supports them in capacity building and resolving disputes.
 
• **Revenue Generation:** Effective management of waqf properties can generate significant revenue, which can be utilized for community welfare and development programs.
 
• **Community Welfare:** Waqf properties are instrumental in funding educational institutions, healthcare facilities, and other welfare initiatives for the Muslim community in India.

questions.question: In May 2025, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has approved the setting up of ______ National Centres of Excellence for Skilling as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2025**, Prime Minister **Shri Narendra Modi** approved the establishment of **5 National Centres of Excellence for Skilling** as a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme**.
 
• The aim of these centers is to enhance **skilling infrastructure** and provide high-quality, industry-relevant training to the youth of India.
 
• The initiative aligns with the **Skill India Mission**, which seeks to equip Indian youth with employable skills and bridge the gap between education and employment.
 
• The scheme is centrally sponsored, meaning the **funding is shared between the central government and state governments**, ensuring collaborative implementation.
 
• The focus of these centers will be on **innovation, technology-driven learning, and industry partnerships** to ensure maximum employability of trained individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Skill India Mission:**

 
 
• Launched by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** in **2015**, the Skill India initiative aims to train over **40 crore individuals** in various skills by **2022**.
 
• It includes programs like **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)** and **National Skill Development Mission**.
 
• The mission focuses on improving **vocational education, skill development, and entrepreneurship opportunities**.
 
 
 
• **National Centres of Excellence for Skilling:**
 
 
• These centers are strategically set up to offer specialized training in emerging sectors such as **Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Renewable Energy, Healthcare, and IT**.
 
• The centers will collaborate with **industry experts** to design curriculum and provide hands-on experience.
 
• The goal is to make India a global hub for **skilled manpower**, supporting economic growth and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Centrally Sponsored Schemes:**
 
 
• A Centrally Sponsored Scheme involves financial contributions from both the **central and state governments**.
 
• Examples include **PMAY (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana)**, **MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act)**, etc.
 
• These schemes aim to promote **development and welfare** across various sectors like **education, health, and infrastructure**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Skilling Initiatives:**
 
 
• India has one of the youngest populations globally, with a median age of **28 years**, making skilling programs critical for **employment generation**.
 
• Skilled manpower contributes to higher productivity, innovation, and economic growth.
 
• Initiatives like these help address challenges such as **unemployment** and **underemployment**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of National Centres of Excellence for Skilling:**

 
 
• Focus on **high-demand sectors** such as **IT, Renewable Energy, Healthcare, and Industry 4.0 technologies**.
 
• Promotes **public-private partnerships** for skill training and job placement.
 
• Emphasizes **hands-on training** to ensure industry readiness.
 
• Supports the **Make in India** and **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiatives by creating a workforce aligned with global demands.
 
 
 
• **Related Government Schemes:**
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY):** Offers free skill training to enhance employability.
 
• **National Skill Development Mission:** Focuses on improving overall skill development infrastructure.
 
• **Skill India Digital Platform:** Provides online learning resources for vocational training.

questions.question: Which sport brought India its first individual Olympic gold?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shooting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's first individual **Olympic gold medal** was won by **Abhinav Bindra** in the sport of **Shooting**. He achieved this historic feat at the **2008 Beijing Olympics**.
 
• Bindra won the gold medal in the **Men's 10m Air Rifle** event, marking a significant moment in India's Olympic history.
 
• This victory made Bindra the first Indian to win an individual gold medal in the Olympics, breaking a long-standing record of India not achieving this feat in the individual categories.
 
• Abhinav Bindra's score in the final was **700.5**, which included a near-perfect performance in the qualifying rounds and the final.
 
• His win brought immense pride to India and inspired the growth of shooting as a popular sport in the country, leading to increased interest and investment in the sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Abhinav Bindra's Background:**

 
 
• He was born on **28 September 1982**, in **Dehradun, Uttarakhand**.
 
• Bindra trained extensively at his private shooting range, which was equipped with advanced technology to simulate international conditions.
 
• He is a graduate of the **University of Colorado**, and his dedication to improving his mental and physical abilities contributed significantly to his success.
 
 
 
• **Shooting Sport in India:**
 
 
• Shooting is governed by the **National Rifle Association of India (NRAI)**, which oversees the development of the sport in the country.
 
• India has been home to several successful shooters, including **Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore** (2004 silver medalist) and **Gagan Narang** (2012 bronze medalist).
 
• The sport has gained popularity over the years, with increased government support and private sponsorships.
 
 
 
• **Other Significant Indian Gold Medalists:**
 
 
• Prior to Bindra's win, India had primarily achieved gold medals in team events, such as Hockey (winning 8 gold medals between 1928 and 1980).
 
• In recent years, athletes like **Neeraj Chopra** (gold in Javelin Throw at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics) have followed in Bindra's footsteps by achieving individual Olympic gold medals.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Bindra's Win:**
 
 
• Bindra's historic win has inspired a new generation of Indian shooters, with many of them achieving success at international events.
 
• It has led to the establishment of specialized shooting academies and increased funding for athletes in the sport.
 
• His autobiography, "**A Shot at History**," chronicles his journey and serves as a motivational guide for aspiring athletes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the 2008 Beijing Olympics:**

 
 
• India's medal tally at the 2008 Olympics included **three medals**: Abhinav Bindra's gold, a bronze by **Vijender Singh** in Boxing, and another bronze by **Sushil Kumar** in Wrestling.
 
• This was India's best-ever performance at the Olympics at that time, marking a turning point for Indian sports on the global stage.
 
 
 
• **Growth of Shooting in India:**
 
 
• Post-2008, shooting has emerged as one of India's strongest sports in international competitions.
 
• India has consistently performed well in events such as the **ISSF World Cups** and **Commonwealth Games**.

questions.question: The MATSYA 6000 is associated with which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deep Ocean Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **MATSYA 6000** is a manned submersible vehicle developed under **India's Deep Ocean Mission**, an initiative by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
 
• This submersible is designed to reach depths of up to **6,000 meters** below sea level, enabling exploration and resource assessment of the deep ocean.
 
• The **Deep Ocean Mission** was launched in **2021** with the aim to harness resources, including polymetallic nodules, from the seabed, particularly in the Indian Ocean.
 
• MATSYA 6000 is equipped with advanced technologies to carry **three crew members** to the depths of the ocean and conduct scientific exploration.
 
• The project aligns with India's aspirations to deepen its research in marine biodiversity, seabed mapping, and resource exploitation, enhancing its status as a leader in ocean research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Deep Ocean Mission:**

 
 
• This mission aims to explore the deep ocean for **minerals, energy, and marine biodiversity**.
 
• The mission includes the development of **technologies for deep-sea mining, underwater vehicles, and underwater robotics**.
 
• The initiative is part of India's efforts to achieve the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 14** (Life Below Water), which focuses on conserving marine resources.
 
• A key focus area of the mission is the **exploration of polymetallic nodules** found in the Central Indian Ocean Basin, which are rich in metals like manganese, nickel, cobalt, and copper.
 
 
 
• **MATSYA 6000:**
 
 
• The submersible is being developed by the **National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT)**, Chennai.
 
• It is equipped with **life support systems** to ensure the safety of scientists for missions lasting up to **12 hours**.
 
• The submersible uses **titanium alloy personnel spheres** to withstand high pressure at extreme depths.
 
• The MATSYA 6000 is expected to play a crucial role in the study of **marine ecosystems** and **geological processes**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Deep Ocean Mission:**
 
 
• Mapping **seabed resources** for potential mining of valuable minerals.
 
• Enhancing understanding of **marine biodiversity** and its conservation.
 
• Strengthening **disaster management capabilities** by studying underwater seismic activity.
 
• Advancing India's research and technology in **underwater robotics**.
 
 
 
• **Other Missions for Context:**
 
 
• **Aditya L-1 Mission:** Focuses on studying the Sun and its atmosphere.
 
• **Shukrayaan Mission:** A proposed mission to study Venus.
 
• **Gaganyaan Mission:** India's first manned space mission, aiming to send astronauts into space.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Deep Ocean Mission** has a budget of **Rs. 4,077 crore** for a five-year period.
 
• India is among a handful of countries, including the US, Japan, and China, that are actively working on **deep-sea exploration technologies**.
 
• The mission's success could help India reduce its dependency on imported **critical minerals**.
 
• It involves collaboration with international organizations under the **United Nations International Seabed Authority (ISA)**.

questions.question: Meenakshi Amman Temple was constructed by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kulasekhara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meenakshi Amman Temple**, located in **Madurai, Tamil Nadu**, is one of the most iconic landmarks in India and is dedicated to **Goddess Meenakshi (a form of Parvati)** and Lord Sundareswarar (a form of Shiva).
 
• The temple was originally constructed during the reign of the **Pandyan king Kulasekhara** in the early centuries of the Common Era.
 
• It underwent major expansions and renovations during the reign of the **Nayak dynasty** in the 16th and 17th centuries, particularly under **Tirumala Nayaka**.
 
• The architectural style of the temple is a blend of **Dravidian architecture**, featuring towering **gopurams**, intricate sculptures, and vibrant frescoes.
 
• The temple complex spans over **14 acres** and includes **14 gopurams** (gateway towers), multiple shrines, and a sacred pond known as **Porthamarai Kulam** (Golden Lotus Tank).
 
• The temple is renowned for its annual **Meenakshi Thirukalyanam** festival, which celebrates the divine marriage of Goddess Meenakshi and Lord Sundareswarar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kulasekhara Dynasty:**

 
 
• The **Pandyan dynasty**, under rulers like Kulasekhara, was one of the three ancient Tamil kingdoms alongside the Chola and Chera dynasties.
 
• They were known for their patronage of **art, architecture, and literature**, particularly in Tamil.
 
• The Pandyan kings were instrumental in promoting **Shaivism and Vaishnavism**, as seen in temples like the Meenakshi Amman Temple.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Architecture:**
 
 
• The Meenakshi Temple is a classic example of **Dravidian architecture**, characterized by **pyramidal gopurams**, ornate carvings, and murals depicting Hindu mythology.
 
• It follows a symmetrical layout and includes **mandapas** (pillared halls), **vimanas** (towering spires over the sanctum), and sacred tanks.
 
 
 
• **Nayak Contributions:**
 
 
• While the original construction was by the Pandyan king Kulasekhara, the Nayak rulers expanded the temple significantly in the **16th century**.
 
• Key features like the **Thousand Pillar Hall** and ornate frescoes were added during this period.
 
• The Nayaks also introduced the iconic **Meenakshi Thirukalyanam festival**, which draws thousands of devotees annually.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Karikala Chola:** Known for his contributions to irrigation and trade, particularly the construction of the **Kallanai Dam**, but not associated with the Meenakshi Temple.
 
• **Pulakeshin I:** A ruler of the Chalukya dynasty, famous for his military conquests, but unrelated to the construction of the temple.
 
• **Narasimha Deva I:** A ruler of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, best known for the **Sun Temple at Konark**, but not linked to the Meenakshi Temple.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Meenakshi Amman Temple is a UNESCO Tentative World Heritage Site, highlighting its cultural and historical significance.
 
• The temple attracts millions of tourists and devotees annually, making it a major pilgrimage site and a symbol of Tamil Nadu's cultural heritage.
 
• Its **sculptures and artwork** depict scenes from Hindu mythology, including the life of Goddess Meenakshi and her marriage to Lord Shiva.
 
• The temple's intricate designs and vibrant colors are a testament to the artistic expertise of ancient Tamil craftsmen.

questions.question: 'Dhamoni Urs Fair' is held in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dhamoni Urs Fair** is a popular annual event held in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**, India.
 
• The fair is organized in the town of **Dhamoni**, located in the Sagar district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• This event is primarily a religious and cultural fair and is dedicated to the memory of revered Sufi saints and their teachings.
 
• Devotees from various parts of Madhya Pradesh and neighboring regions gather to celebrate the Urs, which includes **prayers, Sufi music, and community feasts**.
 
• The fair is also an occasion for local artisans and vendors to showcase their crafts, including traditional Madhya Pradesh handicrafts, food, and other cultural items.
 
• This festival highlights the **spiritual harmony** and cultural heritage of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Religious Importance of Urs:**

 
 
• The term "Urs" is derived from an Arabic word meaning "wedding," symbolizing the union of the soul with the divine.
 
• The Urs festival is typically celebrated at the Dargah (shrine) of a Sufi saint and marks the saint's death anniversary.
 
• It is a time for spiritual reflection, prayers, and the promotion of Sufi teachings of love, peace, and unity.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance of Madhya Pradesh:**
 
 
• Madhya Pradesh, often referred to as the "Heart of India," is renowned for its rich cultural and religious heritage.
 
• The state is home to several fairs and festivals, including the **Khajuraho Dance Festival**, **Tansen Music Festival**, and **Kumbh Mela** in Ujjain.
 
• These events celebrate the state’s diverse traditions, music, dance, and art forms.
 
 
 
• **Other Popular Fairs in Madhya Pradesh:**
 
 
• **Kartik Mela:** Celebrated in Ujjain, this fair is organized during the Kartik month of the Hindu calendar.
 
• **Malwa Utsav:** A cultural festival showcasing the folk dances, music, and crafts of the Malwa region.
 
• **Bhagoria Festival:** A tribal festival celebrated by the Bhil and Bhilala tribes of Madhya Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Tourism in Madhya Pradesh:**
 
 
• The state is famous for its **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**, such as the **Khajuraho Temples**, **Sanchi Stupa**, and **Bhimbetka Rock Shelters**.
 
• It is also home to wildlife sanctuaries and national parks like **Kanha**, **Bandhavgarh**, and **Pench**, which attract nature and wildlife enthusiasts.
 
• Madhya Pradesh offers a blend of spiritual, historical, and natural attractions, making it a unique travel destination.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Location:** Dhamoni is located in the Sagar district of Madhya Pradesh, which is known for its historical significance and cultural richness.
 
• **Connectivity:** Dhamoni is well connected by road, and the nearest railway station is in Sagar, making it accessible for pilgrims and tourists.
 
• **Historical Significance:** Apart from the Urs fair, Dhamoni is known for its ancient fort and architectural heritage, which reflect the region’s history.

questions.question: Which type of satellite is mainly used for weather monitoring and forecasting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geo-stationary satellite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Geo-stationary satellites** are primarily used for **weather monitoring and forecasting**. They are positioned in a fixed orbit above the equator, ensuring they remain over the same geographical location.
 
• These satellites provide **continuous coverage** of the same area, making them ideal for tracking weather patterns, cloud formations, and precipitation.
 
• They operate at an altitude of approximately **35,786 km** above the Earth's surface and match the Earth's rotational speed, ensuring their stationary position relative to the ground.
 
• Geo-stationary satellites are equipped with advanced sensors and cameras to capture **real-time weather data**, including temperature, humidity, wind speed, and atmospheric pressure.
 
• Examples of geo-stationary satellites used for weather forecasting include the **GOES series (USA)**, **INSAT series (India)**, and **Himawari (Japan)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Communication satellites:**

 
 
• These satellites are primarily used for **telecommunication services**, including television broadcasting, internet connectivity, and telephone communication.
 
• They are not designed for weather monitoring but play a significant role in enabling global communication networks.
 
• Examples include the **INTELSAT** and **Iridium** satellite constellations.
 
 
 
• **Reconnaissance satellites:**
 
 
• Also known as **spy satellites**, these are used for military and intelligence purposes, such as **surveillance** and monitoring enemy activities.
 
• They are equipped with high-resolution imaging systems to capture detailed information about specific areas.
 
• Examples include the **KH-11** and **Lacrosse** satellites.
 
 
 
• **Astronomical satellites:**
 
 
• These satellites are designed for **space exploration** and studying celestial objects like stars, galaxies, and planets.
 
• They are equipped with specialized instruments like telescopes, spectrometers, and cameras.
 
• Examples include the **Hubble Space Telescope** and **Chandra X-ray Observatory**.
 
 
 
• **INSAT series (India):**
 
 
• The **INSAT** series of satellites, operated by the Indian Space Research Organisation (**ISRO**), provide a combination of communication, broadcasting, and weather services.
 
• The **INSAT-3D** and **INSAT-3DR** satellites are equipped with advanced payloads for weather monitoring.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geo-stationary satellites' advantages:**

 
 
• Continuous coverage of the same area, enabling real-time data collection.
 
• Ideal for tracking **cyclones, hurricanes**, and other severe weather events.
 
• Supports disaster management by providing early warnings and post-event analysis.
 
 
 
• **Global examples:**
 
 
• **GOES series** (USA): Managed by NOAA for weather forecasting and monitoring.
 
• **Himawari series** (Japan): Operated by the Japan Meteorological Agency (**JMA**).
 
• **Meteosat** (Europe): Operated by EUMETSAT for weather and climate studies.

questions.question: Mechanical energy is mainly composed of how many types?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mechanical energy** is primarily classified into **two types: kinetic energy and potential energy.**
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the energy an object possesses due to its motion. For example, a moving car or a flowing river has kinetic energy.
 
• **Potential energy** is the energy an object possesses due to its position or configuration. For instance, water stored in a dam at height or a stretched spring has potential energy.
 
• The sum of kinetic and potential energy in a system constitutes its total **mechanical energy.**
 
• This classification of mechanical energy into two types is widely accepted in physics and forms the basis for understanding energy transfer in mechanical systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**

 
 
• Mathematically, kinetic energy is expressed as KE=12mv2" id="MathJax-Element-6-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">KE=12mv2KE=12mv2" id="MathJax-Element-1-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">KE=12mv2KE=12mv2
 KE=12mv2
 KE = \frac{1}{2}mv² , where **m** is the mass of the object and **v** is its velocity.
 
• Kinetic energy is directly proportional to the mass and square of the velocity, meaning an increase in either will increase the kinetic energy.
 
• Examples include moving vehicles, flying airplanes, and running athletes.
 
 
 
• **Potential Energy:**
 
 
• Potential energy is calculated using the formula PE=mgh" id="MathJax-Element-7-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">PE=mghPE=mgh" id="MathJax-Element-2-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">PE=mghPE=mgh
 PE=mgh
 PE = mgh , where **m** is the mass, **g** is the acceleration due to gravity, and **h** is the height.
 
• It depends on the object's position relative to a reference point, such as the height of an object above the ground.
 
• Examples include water stored in a dam, a compressed spring, or a pendulum at its highest point.
 
 
 
• **Energy Conversion:**
 
 
• Mechanical energy can transform between kinetic and potential energy. For example, in a pendulum, energy constantly shifts between these two forms.
 
• In a roller coaster, the mechanical energy is conserved as the cars move up and down the tracks, swapping kinetic energy for potential energy and vice versa.
 
 
 
• **Real-World Applications:**
 
 
• Mechanical energy is utilized in various machines, engines, and systems such as wind turbines, hydropower plants, and mechanical clocks.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in engineering, physics, and various technological applications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation of Mechanical Energy:**

 
 
• Mechanical energy is conserved in an isolated system where only conservative forces (like gravity) are acting.
 
• This principle is fundamental to solving many physics problems, such as calculating the motion of a projectile or the dynamics of a pendulum.
 
 
 
• **Non-Conservative Forces:**
 
 
• When non-conservative forces like friction or air resistance act on a system, mechanical energy is not conserved, as some energy is converted into heat or other forms.
 
• This explains why a rolling ball eventually comes to a stop or why energy losses occur in real-world machines.

questions.question: In the context of Budget, which of the following is NOT an example of capital expenditure of government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subsidies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capital expenditure** refers to spending by the government on assets that have a long-term utility and contribute to the economic growth of the country. Examples include acquiring land, investing in infrastructure, and creating development projects.
 
• **Subsidies**, on the other hand, are classified as **revenue expenditure** because they are recurring payments made by the government to support specific sectors, individuals, or industries and do not create long-term assets. *Hence, subsidies are NOT considered capital expenditure.*
 
• Expenditures such as **acquisition of land**, **investment in shares**, and constructing buildings for development are capital expenditures as they result in the creation of physical or financial assets.
 
• Revenue expenditure, including subsidies, is focused on maintaining the daily functioning of the government or providing immediate economic support rather than creating enduring economic value.
 
• Subsidies are a form of financial assistance provided by the government to reduce the cost of goods or services, ensuring affordability for certain sectors or the public. They do not contribute to the creation of permanent assets.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Subsidies.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Capital expenditure:**

 
 
• Capital expenditure is incurred by the government for acquiring assets such as land, buildings, machinery, equipment, or investments that contribute to long-term economic benefits.
 
• Examples include infrastructure development, setting up industries, and acquiring physical or financial assets.
 
• It is non-recurring in nature and reflects in the country’s balance sheet, improving its economic capacity.
 
• **Investment in shares:** Investing in shares by the government is considered capital expenditure as it leads to the creation of financial assets that may provide future returns.
 
 
 
• **Revenue expenditure:**
 
 
• Revenue expenditure refers to expenses incurred for the day-to-day running of government operations and services.
 
• It includes payments such as salaries, interest payments, subsidies, and welfare schemes. These expenditures are recurring and do not contribute to asset creation.
 
• **Subsidies:** Subsidies are a classic example of revenue expenditure. These financial aids are provided to support sectors such as agriculture, education, health, and industry.
 
• Subsidies are aimed at reducing the cost burden on citizens or businesses but do not result in the creation of physical or financial assets.
 
 
 
• **Building for development:** Constructing buildings for development purposes is classified under capital expenditure because it involves the creation of infrastructure that contributes to economic growth.
 
• **Fiscal policy:** The classification of expenditure into capital and revenue categories is critical for fiscal policy. Governments aim to balance these expenditures to ensure economic growth while maintaining fiscal discipline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key characteristics of capital and revenue expenditure:**

 
 
• **Capital expenditure:** Non-recurring, creates assets, contributes to long-term economic benefits.
 
• **Revenue expenditure:** Recurring, supports day-to-day government functions, does not create assets.
 
 
 
• **Government budget classifications:** The classification of expenditure is critical in understanding how the government allocates resources and prioritizes economic development versus operational needs.
 
• **Economic significance:** Capital expenditure boosts economic growth by creating infrastructure, while revenue expenditure ensures smooth functioning and immediate welfare benefits.

questions.question: The members of Rajya Sabha are elected for a term of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **members of the Rajya Sabha** are elected for a term of **6 years**. This is outlined in the **Constitution of India**.
 
• One-third of the members of the Rajya Sabha retire every two years, ensuring a **continuous rotation** of its membership.
 
• Unlike the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha is **not subject to dissolution**. It is a permanent body and continues to exist, with vacancies being filled periodically.
 
• The Rajya Sabha, also referred to as the **Upper House of Parliament**, represents the states and union territories of India.
 
• The **election process for the Rajya Sabha** members is indirect. Members are elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the states and union territories through a system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rajya Sabha Composition:**

 
 
• The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is **250 members**, out of which **238 are elected** and **12 are nominated** by the President of India.
 
• The nominated members are chosen for their expertise in fields such as **literature, science, art, and social services**.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria for Rajya Sabha Membership:**
 
 
• A candidate must be at least **30 years old** to contest elections for the Rajya Sabha.
 
• He/she must be an Indian citizen and fulfill other criteria set forth by the **Representation of the People Act, 1951**.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha’s Role:**
 
 
• It acts as the **Council of States** and provides representation to states and union territories.
 
• The Rajya Sabha plays a significant role in **legislative matters**, except for money bills, which can only originate in the Lok Sabha.
 
• It serves as a check on the Lok Sabha and ensures representation of regional interests at the national level.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• The **Lok Sabha** (Lower House) is directly elected by the people, whereas the **Rajya Sabha** is indirectly elected by the state legislatures.
 
• The Lok Sabha has a term of **5 years**, while the Rajya Sabha is a **permanent body**.
 
• The Lok Sabha is larger, with a maximum strength of **552 members**, compared to the Rajya Sabha's **250 members**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Proportional Representation System:**

 
 
• The members of the Rajya Sabha are elected through the **proportional representation** system via the **single transferable vote**.
 
• This system ensures that minority groups also get representation in the Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **President’s Role in Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• The **Vice President of India** serves as the **ex-officio Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The President of India nominates **12 members** to the Rajya Sabha based on their contribution to various fields.

questions.question: What is the primary function of hydrochloric acid in the stomach of humans?

options.text: To create an acidic medium for enzyme action

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To create an acidic medium for enzyme action**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** in the stomach creates an **acidic medium**, which is essential for the activation of the enzyme **pepsin.** Pepsin is responsible for the digestion of proteins into smaller peptides.
 
• The pH level in the stomach due to HCl is approximately **1.5 to 3.5**, which is highly acidic. This environment is optimal for the functioning of digestive enzymes.
 
• HCl also helps in the **denaturation of proteins**, which means it unfolds the protein structures, making them more accessible for enzymatic breakdown.
 
• Another important role of HCl is to act as a **defense mechanism** by killing harmful bacteria and pathogens present in the food, thereby preventing infections.
 
• It does not neutralize food or create an alkaline medium; instead, it ensures an acidic environment for proper digestion. Hence, options 1 and 2 are incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of Hydrochloric Acid:**

 
 
• It activates **pepsinogen** (an inactive precursor) into its active form, pepsin, which is crucial for protein digestion.
 
• It breaks down the bonds between food particles, making nutrients more accessible for absorption in the intestine.
 
• The acidic environment facilitates the absorption of certain nutrients, such as **iron and calcium**, which require an acidic medium for solubilization.
 
 
 
• **Enzymes in Digestion:**
 
 
• **Pepsin:** Works in the acidic medium to break down proteins into smaller peptides.
 
• **Amylase:** Though it starts carbohydrate digestion in the mouth, its activity is halted in the stomach due to the acidic pH.
 
• **Lipase:** Functions to a limited extent in the stomach to break down fats.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Stomach:**
 
 
• Acts as a temporary reservoir where food is mixed with gastric juices.
 
• Releases small amounts of food (chyme) into the small intestine for further digestion and absorption.
 
• Produces intrinsic factors necessary for the absorption of **Vitamin B12** in the small intestine.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Information:**
 
 
• Conditions like **hypochlorhydria** (low stomach acid) can impair digestion and lead to nutrient deficiencies.
 
• Excessive production of HCl may cause conditions like **acid reflux** or ulcers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Neutralization of Food:** This is incorrect as food is not neutralized in the stomach; instead, it is acidified by HCl for enzymatic action.
 
• **Alkaline Medium:** The stomach does not create an alkaline medium; the small intestine creates an alkaline environment for further digestion.
 
• **Protein Digestion:** Proteins begin to break down in the stomach due to the acidic environment and the action of pepsin.
 
• **Bacteria and Pathogens:** The acidic pH of the stomach is effective in killing many harmful organisms, reducing the risk of infections.
 
• **Absorption of Nutrients:** Certain nutrients such as iron and calcium rely on the acidic environment of the stomach for proper absorption.
